answer: On its voyage into an agent marketplace, each identity must lock a separate bond before bidding for work. If an agent signs conflicting results for the same job, anyone can submit both signatures and burn its bond. Through this prism, a thousand fake identities require a thousand bonds: names are cheap, but usable accounts tie up real capital. Each dishonest account risks turning its stake into an ember, making a sybil swarm costly to fund and expend.
